scores.claim_text: 310 data centers across 7 regions, ~57.6M rsf, 84.7% leased as of 12/31/2025.
supports: EDGAR fulltext: 'Digital Realty' returns 1,583 hits across 8-K/10-K/10-Q since 2018, consistent with continuous, granular property-level disclosure typical of mature global REIT.
DLR 10-K filed 2026-02-13 itemizes properties metro-by-metro in Item 2 with sq ft and occupancy %; no rounding inconsistencies.
scores.interpretation: Routine REIT property-portfolio disclosure with deep filing trail. No discriminative red flag. Calibration heuristic 3 N/A (operational, not planned).

scores.claim_text: 769 MW underway, 64% pre-leased; 2.9 GW in-place IT capacity; 5 GW future capacity.
supports: EDGAR fulltext '769 megawatts' returns 1 hit — the DLR 10-K itself (no other issuer plagiarizing or contradicting the number).
Stage ladder is properly broken out (operational vs under-construction vs future development capacity) per heuristic 3.
Pre-lease percentage (64%) disclosed transparently — discrimines from term-sheet/MOU stage to lease stage.
scores.interpretation: Properly staged capacity disclosure that distinguishes operating / under construction / future. No TCV-vs-recognized-revenue conflation (heuristic 9). Mature DC-REIT disclosure quality.

scores.claim_text: Oracle = #2 customer at $424M ARR (9.0%), 42 locations, 10.2yr WALT.
supports: Oracle is named explicitly (not behind 'Global Cloud Provider' descriptor).
Oracle 10-Ks (FY19-FY25, 7 filings) mention 'colocation' in their data-center capacity discussion — counterparty-side language consistent with leasing relationship.
$424M ARR at the customer's $50B+ revenue level is not individually material to Oracle (~0.8%), so heuristic 7 absence-of-named-disclosure threshold is NOT triggered.
WALT 10.2yr indicates definitive lease, not MOU.
scores.M_value: DLR-name hits in ORCL: 0; 'colocation' hits in ORCL: 8 (FY18-FY25 10-Ks)
scores.interpretation: Hyperscalers generally do not name landlords in 10-K (commercially confidential); Oracle's repeated colocation discussion is the expected corroboration. Below counterparty-disclosure threshold of heuristic 7.

scores.claim_text: Meta Platforms = #8 customer, 49 locations, $73.5M ARR (1.6%), 2.8yr WALT.
supports: Meta named explicitly with location count and WALT.
$73.5M ARR is tiny relative to Meta capex; far below disclosure-materiality threshold under heuristic 7.
Shorter WALT (2.8yr) consistent with Meta's stated build-own preference for new sites with colocation as bridging capacity.
scores.M_value: 0 hits — below materiality threshold; expected null result.
scores.interpretation: Per calibration heuristic 7 exception: counterparty-side absence not a red flag when claim sub-threshold. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Largest customer (unnamed 'Fortune 50 Software Company') = 11.7% of ARR, $547M, 76 locations, 9.4yr WALT.
supports: Disclosed as 'Fortune 50 Software Company' descriptor (commonly understood = Microsoft) — consistent with hyperscaler-customer NDAs.
11.7% concentration is disclosed transparently (not hidden behind aggregate buckets).
9.4yr WALT signals definitive long-term lease, not MOU; not subject to heuristic 3 stage-ladder concern.

Cross-checks: MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL 10-Ks have 0 hits for 'Digital Realty' — but per heuristic 7 hyperscalers routinely do not name landlords in 10-K narratives even when leases are material to DLR side; absence on counterparty side is consistent with industry norm, not a contradiction.
DLR has aggregate lease-distribution disclosures (>1MW deployments = 59.7% of ARR) and lease-expiration ladder that reconciles to the customer table.
scores.interpretation: Counterparty-side silence on landlord identity is the industry norm; absence does not contradict an existing operational lease relationship. Sub-threshold under heuristic 7 (hyperscaler 10-K capex commentary references unnamed colocation providers, not specific landlords). PASS — but flagged as a structural disclosure-blind spot inherent to the AI-DC space.

scores.claim_text: Jan 2024 Blackstone JV: 4 hyperscale campuses, 10 data centers, ~500 MW, $3.0B Phase 1 cost; DLR retained 20%.
supports: Counterparty Blackstone (CIK 0001393818) filed an 8-K dated 2024-01-25 with an exhibit confirming the Digital Realty JV — independent EDGAR corroboration from the named partner.
DLR 10-K transparently splits Phase 1 / Phase 2, identifies proceeds ($231M + $385M), discloses gain/loss on derecognition.
$3.0B development cost is properly tagged as future investment, not current revenue (heuristic 9 satisfied).
scores.interpretation: Strong bi-directional corroboration of named partnership claim. Clean disclosure with proper accounting splits.

scores.claim_text: Cash $3.45B; total debt $18.56B (78% fixed-rate incl swaps); FY26 capex guide $3.25-$3.75B.
supports: DLR is investment-grade rated, has $4.5B undrawn Global Revolving Credit Facility maturing 2029.
Net debt / 2025 Adj EBITDA target ratio 5.5x with floating-rate cap at 20% — standard mature REIT capital structure.
DLR raised $4.8B equity capital 2024-2025; balance-sheet capacity easily covers $3.5B/yr capex plan.
No distress markers (no Form 15, no reverse split, no going-concern qualifier, no large dilutive convertible).
scores.M_check: Internal MD&A + EDGAR filings index review
scores.M_value: Investment grade; ample revolver; no distress markers
scores.interpretation: Per heuristic 10, none of the delisting / going-concern fingerprints present. Mature scaled REIT with predictable lease-based cash flows. PASS.

scores.claim_text: >3,500 MW future capacity in land bank, including >1,000 MW developable in Northern Virginia.
supports: Land-bank claim is supported by 9.7M sq ft active development + 4.7M sq ft held-for-development in the Item 2 property table, which is metro-by-metro itemized.

Northern Virginia portfolio alone = 16 owned + 15 unconsolidated buildings with 3,581k + 5,200k sq ft, plus 2,325k + 309k sq ft held/active development — physically consistent with >1,000 MW build potential at modern DC density.
Patent corroboration: USPTO ODP returns 3 granted patents (Pervasive Data Center Architecture) — light estate, expected per heuristic 8, not a red flag.
scores.interpretation: Land/MW math reconciles with itemized property table. No conflict between marketing language and audited disclosures. PASS.
